incidente.resumo: At a water treatment plant, the fluoride feed pump was accidentally commanded to an 80 percent feed rate; a correction about twelve seconds later did not register, and the pump appears to have run well above the commanded speed for about 3.25 hours, producing a fluoride overfeed. The extra fluoride dosage plus a water main break the next day prompted a water shortage, and customers could not use or drink their water for more than 24 hours. The text does not say how the overfeed was corrected.
servicos_afetados: OWASA water supply (Orange County, Chapel Hill and Carrboro)

descricao.texto: A lead operator at the plant noticed the extra high fluoride levels.
trechos: A lead operator at the plant noticed the extra high levels "but did not take corrective action, leading to the issue not being resolved until after 2:40 p.m."

gatilho.texto: At 11:43 a.m. on February 2, the plant's fluoride feed pump was accidentally instructed to increase its feed rate to 80 percent, compared with its normal operating range of about 8–12 percent.
trechos: According to the fluoride report, by CH2M HILL North Carolina, at 11:43 a.m. on February 2, a plant operator accidentally instructed the plant's fluoride feed pump to increase its feed rate to 80 percent, compared with its normal operating range of about 8–12 percent.

descricao.texto: An attempt to change the command about twelve seconds later did not register, according to the report; the pump appears to have operated at a rate significantly greater than the subsequent commanded speed for approximately 3.25 hours, resulting in a fluoride overfeed condition. The text does not explain why the correction did not register.
trechos: The operator tried to change the command about twelve seconds later, but according to the report, the change didn't register.
"The pump appears to have operated at a rate significantly greater than the subsequent commanded speed for approximately 3.25 hours, resulting in a fluoride overfeed condition," the report says.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: According to the report, the extra high levels were noticed at the plant but corrective action was not taken, leading to the issue not being resolved until after 2:40 p.m.
trechos: A lead operator at the plant noticed the extra high levels "but did not take corrective action, leading to the issue not being resolved until after 2:40 p.m."

fatores_contribuintes.texto: A major water main break the next day, together with the extra fluoride dosage, prompted a water shortage in Orange County; the break leaked about 1.2 million gallons and caused system pressure to plummet, so customers were ordered not to use or drink their water.
trechos: The extra fluoride dosage, plus a major water main break the next day, prompted a water shortage in Orange County that closed businesses, placed Chapel Hill and Carrboro under states of emergency, and sent residents scrambling to buy bottled water.
The break leaked about 1.2 million gallons of water, causing pressure in the system to plummet.
As a result, customers were ordered not to use or drink their water because low flow can allow bacteria to grow in pipes.

acoes.texto: Planned: the OWASA Board agreed that OWASA would develop solutions to prevent the particular failures, assess outage risks more broadly, take action to improve water system resiliency, and review communication practices during critical events.
trechos: Last night, the Board agreed that OWASA would develop solutions to prevent the particular failures of last week, assess outage risks more broadly and take action to improve the water system resiliency, and review communication practices of OWASA and its partners during critical events.

acoes.texto: Already done: OWASA says it has stopped adding fluoride to the water; according to The News & Observer, it is reviewing its policies and seeking public input before reintroducing it.
trechos: OWASA says it has stopped adding fluoride to the water, and
reports that the agency is reviewing its policies and seeking public input before reintroducing it to the water supply.
